fix: The class is a claimed provenance with no check against the log. `--by judge`: require the latest `reframe-verdict` of a review in the finding's lineage to be `accepted`, with no `overturns`, and with this finding in its reframe's `removes`. Refuse otherwise, in dispose, and block it in the gate as well. `--by user`: keep it, but record and show it as the user's call. Check that the 'accepted but overturns' path cannot be recorded as `--by judge`.
text: `dispose --reframed ... --by judge` is accepted on the driver's word: reframe_check only regex-matches `--by` against ^(judge|user)\b, and verdict-gate.py:153 applies the same regex. Neither looks for a `reframe-verdict` record with verdict `accepted` whose reframe `removes` this finding, so the 'fresh judge, never the driver' property from scope §4.2 / Task 2.2 is not enforced anywhere. A driver can dispose any finding, blocking included, as `reframed --by judge` with any post-review commit. The gate then counts it like a deferral, and /verify never audits it as a rejection. The only backstop is that some later review's range contains the commit, which never checks that the original finding went away. The same applies to an accepted reframe that `overturns` a recorded decision: the [REFRAME] stop is printed text only, and `--by judge` still passes.

fix: Version the lineage rule the way decision 65 versions the loop rules. A review record without `rules_version` >= 2 keeps the old `base == phead` continuation, so closed units' stops stand. Apply the fix-sha test only to stamped records. Add a regression test with a pre-cutover log in the 194.1 shape: an accept-stop at old round 3 still satisfies the gate.
text: The lineage fix applies retroactively to every existing review log, and only rules_version is versioned (decision 65), not the lineage rule. I re-ran the gate, old vs new, over all 299 review logs under ~/Projects. Archived unit kalpa-docs 194.1 gains `BLOCK rereview:194.1-r7-01`. Under the old rule, r6 (base == r5's head) continued r5 → r7 was round 3 → capped, and the recorded `accept` stood in for the re-review. Under the new rule r5 has no `fixed` disposition, so r6 roots a new lineage, r7 is round 2, and the stop no longer stands. 11 logs change `capped` membership in total. Second failure mode: for base == phead the old code decided without git, but `_range_holds` now runs `git rev-list` and returns None when history is pruned or unreadable. The review is then 'unsure' and joins the repo's highest-round lineage. On 149.2 this moves r36 from round 2 to 8 and r23 from 3 to 5, and in principle it can merge an unrelated lineage into a capped one.

fix: Either have record stamp the effort codex-exec was actually given (pass it through), or print a WARN from prepare when it ran without --scope/--unit that the effort shown assumes rules 2.
text: `prepare` without --scope/--unit assumes round 1 and RULES_VERSION. So `effort:` prints the trial-bumped tier even for a lineage rooted before the cutover, which decision 65 says keeps its own effort. `record` (with --scope) recomputes `effort`/`effort_base` from the lineage's real rules and not from the tier codex actually ran at. The stamp the scorecard compares can therefore disagree with the run.

fix: Separate the decision from the emission. Classify (overturns or reframe_door, with any exception from door.classify treated as one-way) before printing the accepted line. When it is Alex's call, print the hold line ('do not build until answered: packet or inline question') in place of 'build it', whatever happens to the emission. Then try the packet. Add a test where emission fails on a door-touching accepted reframe and assert stdout never says 'build it'.
text: Case 1 (accepted reframe touching a one-way door, no overturns) is fail-open. reframe-record first prints the plain accepted line `[REFRAME] … accepted … build it, then record each finding it replaced`, and only afterwards, and only if packet_overturn() succeeds in writing a packet, prints `do not build it until the packet is answered`. Whether this is a door case is computed inside the emission, so any emission failure loses the classification too: packet_for returns None when the repo is not under VERIFY_PROJECTS, packet.py exits non-zero (outbox unwritable, schema refusal), or door.classify raises (it is called without a guard inside reframe_door). Each of these leaves stdout saying 'build it' and a generic stderr warning. Even on success, stdout carries both 'build it' and 'do not build it'. Scope §4.2 sends a door-touching accepted reframe to Alex, and the 10.2 fix discipline says new guards fail closed. The emission-failure test covers only case 2 via record, not reframe-record.

fix: Record the reviewed repo's actual path (the --repo argument record already has) and pass it to packet_for in place of the PROJECTS reconstruction, or have cmd_record/cmd_reframe_record pass a.repo through. Pass --range base..head so the packet ties to the reviewed head.
text: The packet's repo is os.path.join(vl.PROJECTS, e['repo']), and e['repo'] is repo_key(main_worktree(...)): the primary checkout, not the worktree that was reviewed. packet.py new runs with cwd set to that primary checkout. So for every herdr lane (concurrency worktrees, the main use case of scope 10), the packet lands in the primary checkout's .decision-queue/outbox, and its `branch` and `head_sha` record whatever the primary checkout has checked out (usually main), not the lane's reviewed head. A repo outside ~/Projects falls back to its basename under PROJECTS, which can resolve to an unrelated repo with the same name. The verify side uses os.getcwd(), so the two emitters disagree about where a packet goes.

fix: Run repeated_reframe before the [REFRAME] judge-it line. On a repeat, replace that line with the hold (Alex's call, do not re-judge), and have reframe-prepare refuse (or warn on) a reframe that repeated_reframe matches.
text: For case 3, record prints `[REFRAME] … judge it before fixing them — review.py reframe-prepare …` and then a `[PACKET] … repeat case — Alex's call` line for the same review. review/SKILL.md says case 3 is emitted 'before any re-judging', and §4.2 says a reframe already rejected and proposed again is Alex's to see, not the loop's to re-judge (repeated_reframe's docstring says the same). Nothing in reframe-prepare refuses a repeat, though, and the stdout tells the driver to re-judge. A re-judge that accepts would then proceed to build while the packet waits.

fix: Either narrow round-3 stuck to blocking findings whose file or lineage carried a blocking finding in an earlier round, or state in §4.2/SKILL that round-3-no-SHIP counts as survival. Reword both docstrings to say 'fails open (no packet) because …', with the reason.
text: Case 2 fires on any blocking finding in a round 3 or later review with no SHIP, including a defect first raised in round 3. The plan and §4.2 say 'a blocking finding that survived two rounds'. The SKILL text documents the wider reading ('round 3 or later with no SHIP'), so this is a definition drift, not a hidden one. Separately, the docstrings of packet_stuck ('Fail-closed: an unknown round is round 0, so it never fires early') and repeated_reframe ('Fails closed toward a packet: … no proposal text is not a repeat') call fail-closed behaviour that is fail-open: an unknown input produces no packet.

Because reframe_call recomputes the repeat on every call, a reframe the judge accepted and the loop built (stamped user_call=None, findings disposed --reframed --by judge) flips to call 'user' / kind 'repeat' as soon as a LATER review in the lineage proposes something >=0.85 similar and the judge rejects it (e.g. 'already built').
